standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of finite products of abelian groups and products in the derived category
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, the lemma that a finite product of exact sequences of abelian groups is exact, and Derived Categories, the lemma describing products in the derived category, together with the definition of the derived limit

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 13837-13857): one direction evaluates the sequence at any weakly contractible U; conversely, if a section s of F_2 lies in the kernel and {U_i -> V} is a covering by elements of B, each s|U_i lifts to F_1(U_i), so s is a section of the image sheaf and the sequence is exact.
Part (2) (proof line 13859): the identification of K with the derived limit of its canonical truncations is the limit-dimension lemma with d = 0.

Part (3) (proof lines 13861-13870): for U in B the limit of the F_n(U) surjects onto F_1(U) because the transition maps are surjective, and surjectivity of the map of sheaves follows from the covering assumption.

Part (4) (proof lines 13872-13892): apply criterion (1): products of sections are products of the sections, and a product of exact sequences of abelian groups is exact, so the product sequence is exact on all U in B and hence exact.

Parts (5), (6) and (7) (proof lines 13894-13918): part (5) follows from (4) and the (slightly generalized) lemma on products in the derived category; for (6) and (7) use the distinguished triangle R lim K_n -> prod K_n -> prod K_n -> R lim K_n[1], take the long exact cohomology sequence, simplify it with exactness of products from (4), and apply the result first to K_n = F_n[0] for (6) and then to the general system for (7).
proof_roadmap: Test exactness on the basis and lift locally using coverings by basis elements, giving criteria (1) and (4).
Read part (2) off the limit-dimension lemma and part (3) off surjectivity on the basis.
Use the defining triangle of the derived limit together with exactness of products to obtain (5), (6) and (7).
difficulty_reason: The proposition collects the consequences of having a basis of weakly contractible objects on a ringed site: exactness can be tested on the basis, all objects of the derived category are derived limits of their truncations, inverse limits with surjective transitions stay surjective, products are exact in the module category and computed termwise in the derived category, and the derived limit functors are described in terms of products with the usual short exact sequences (statement lines 13800-13834). The proof (proof lines 13836-13918) uses the exactness of sections over weakly contractible objects for the criterion, the limit-dimension lemma for the truncation statement, local lifting for the surjectivity statement, and the defining triangle of the derived limit plus exactness of products for the derived statements. H2: seven short arguments with named inputs, all written out.
